items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: James Baldwin wrote a powerful response to James Lincoln Collier’s The Making of Jazz which was published in 1979, James Lincoln Collier the prominent writer who graduated from Hamilton College in 1952.

ctx.x: Well I — what I think is we should — I’m really glad that you’re going to be able to make the “Traditions Transformation” presentation. Because out of this interview, you know I could talk story, music story, for a long time. So I think it’s more like I need to show you more of what I’m doing and then that’s going to come up with some other questions. Now whether I directly address them or maybe I take an improvisation in another direction — and I am improvising. I mean of course it’s all a lot of content…

talk about, but it doesn’t — I’m not sure it really expresses who I am. So and we can’t go into the whole — I mean I already spent too much time on my childhood, about the railroad. But yet, actually, let me put it another way. If you’re interested, on YouTube I recently was awarded the History Maker award by the Chinese Historical Society of America, last month. That was September 21st. And they did a three minute YouTube, or a three or four minute YouTube. And I open up where I saw well I’m just like my father,…

Well this has been fascinating, once again. And I wish you the best of luck with your concert on Friday, and as a pianist and composer and thinker — and I think you called yourself a “cultural entrepreneur?”
